chunks: As for what was narrated by 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon them both):

He said: When you have dried the deceased, proceed to the camphor and rub it on the marks of prostration and all of his joints; and place in his mouth, his ears, his head, and his beard some hanut, as well as upon his chest and his private parts. And he said: The hanut for a man and a woman is the same.
The ruling on this matter is also identical to what we stated in the first hadith.

key_terms.آثَارَ: marks/traces — specifically the seven prostration points on the body of the deceased
key_terms.الْحَنُوطِ: hanut — scenting compound placed in the mouth, ears, head, beard, chest, and private parts of the deceased
key_terms.الْكَافُورِ: camphor — fragrant white substance rubbed on the deceased's prostration marks and joints
key_terms.مَفَاصِلَهُ: his joints — all articulations of the body

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method of applying camphor and hanut to a deceased person according to Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq (peace be upon them)?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Zurara from Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq (peace be upon them both), prescribes the ritual application of camphor (kafur) to the marks of prostration and all joints of the deceased, and hanut to the mouth, ears, head, beard, chest, and private parts. It further establishes that the hanut treatment is uniform for both men and women. Sheikh al-Tusi concludes that the jurisprudential ruling here is identical to what was stated in the preceding hadith.
